source_title: A Generalization of Zwegers' mu-Function According to the q-Hermite-Weber Difference Equation
title: The q-Borel plus q-Laplace image of the q-Hermite-Weber fundamental solution equals the generalized mu-function

standard_prerequisites: The series definition of the generalized mu-function def:mua (1.1, source lines 343-362), the value the proof identifies at the end.

The fundamental solution of the q-Hermite-Weber equation as the 2phi0 series t-tilde-f_0 (source lines 365-369) and the q-Laplace transformation eq:q-Laplace (1.21, source line 331) composing it into f_0.
The q-binomial theorem, cited at line 747 from entry GR (p. 8, equation (1.3.2)), a standard published input used to sum the q-Borel image.
core_obligations: Theorem 1.2, eq:mu and q-Hermite--Weber (1.22, label line 379): f_0(e^(2 pi i (u-v)), -e^(2 pi i u)) = mu(u,v;alpha), i.e. the image of the composition of the q-Borel and q-Laplace transformations of the fundamental solution is essentially the generalized mu-function.
proof_roadmap: Sum the q-Borel image B+(f-tilde_0) as a quotient of q-Pochhammer symbols by the q-binomial theorem (source lines 748-753).
Compose the q-Laplace transform and reduce the theta sum by the q-difference relation theta_q(q^n x) = q^(-n(n-1)/2) x^(-n) theta_q(x), displayed in-span (source lines 757-767).

Substitute x = e^(2 pi i (u-v)) and lambda = -e^(2 pi i u) (source lines 768-776) and re-index the sum by n -> n+1/2 to match the defining series of mu (source lines 776-778): the display closes with i q^(1/8) mu(u,v;alpha), the author's tag-qed device included.
